notes: **2026-09-02 (mechanical remainder pass — the 9 items handed off after the concurrency/safety pass)** — (branch `feat/bug-registry`, PR #597; `scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs` + `scripts/campaign-check.mjs` + a new `scripts/campaign/reg-token.mjs` + SKILL.md, 8 fix commits, one per numbered item; self-test 181 → 204 checks) — **NOT lock/catalogue/occupancy/injection/pagination (those were already fixed by the prior pass) — the remaining mechanical minors/majors.** (1) `prove --build-plan` REJECTS an absolute or `../`-escaping path (`isAbsolute`, `relative(REPO_ROOT,…)`) instead of persisting it verbatim — an absolute path leaked a local username into the tracked shard and turned campaign-check red on every other machine; the normalised, forward-slash, repo-relative form is what gets stored now. (2) `discharge`'s byte-identical-evidence guard now seeds `seen` from every existing `dischargeEvidence` across ALL shards, not just the current call's rows — it is per-batch while the guard claims to be ledger-wide, so the same string reused across two separate `discharge` calls used to sail through both and campaign-check had to call the second one "grandfathered" instead of refusing it. (3) New `scripts/campaign/reg-token.mjs` (`REG_TOKEN_RE` = 1-4 digits, `hasRegToken`, `manualVerificationIds`/`hasManualVerificationRow`) replaces what a comment called "a literal duplicate" between `prove`'s T3 check (any digit count) and campaign-check's gate (exactly 2-3 digits) — a single-digit id could be proven but never discharged; the shared function also requires the token to sit in a TABLE ROW (`/^\s*\|/`) of the "## Manual verification" section after stripping fenced code blocks, identically on both sides — a token merely mentioned in prose, or inside a fence saying not to use it, no longer counts. (4) `file`'s catch now drops the ledger row it just added (new `dropLedgerRow`, under the shard lock) alongside the existing catalogue restore — the row used to survive as an ORPHAN with no catalogue entry and no record, invisible to every gate; a new self-test integrity check fails on any ledger row with no matching catalogue row. (5) `discharge` snapshots the shard file before its row loop and restores it whole on any throw — an IO failure mid-batch used to leave half the batch `done` and half `proven` with no rollback, and exit with a raw Node stack trace; the CLI entry point now wraps `cmds[cmd](rest)` so any exception `fail()` didn't anticipate prints one `bugs: unexpected failure in <cmd> — …` line instead (`BUGS_DEBUG=1` still shows the real stack). (6) `computeWaves` fills the holes in its sparse `waves` array with an explicit index loop instead of `.map`-ing over them (which SKIPS holes) — `waves[0]` used to serialise as `null`, not `[]`, whenever busy batches alone filled the agent cap. (7) `next`'s text output now prints EVERY wave-1 batch's own `claimCheck`, not just the head's — the rest of wave 1 used to be listed as "safe to run alongside it" with no warning even when their checks failed identically. (8) `selectBatches` tags each busy skip with `busyWhy` (`"in-flight"` | `"leased"`) so `blocked`'s reason renders `blocked by leased F##` when the holder is a remote `team.mjs` lease with no local in-flight row at all, instead of hardcoding "in-flight" for both. (9) INVESTIGATED, no code change: the earlier claim that `scripts/team/team.mjs` "gained a comment block only" is false — `git show 00d53223:scripts/team/team.mjs | npx prettier --check` fails, so master's copy was NOT prettier-clean and the dozens of reformat hunks in the diff are the pre-commit hook's doing, unavoidable on any touch that lands a commit (never bypass the hook to "fix" this).
